output.content:
**Mobileye (NASDAQ: MBLY)** is an autonomous-driving and advanced driver-assistance systems (ADAS) company; its core technologies include EyeQ chips, computer vision, mapping, and software designed for driver assistance and progressively more autonomous vehicles. [[1]]

- **Revenue:** For the fiscal year ended December 27, 2025, Mobileye reported consolidated revenue of **$1.894 billion**, up **15%** from **$1.654 billion** in FY2024. [[2]]
- **Autonomous-driving/ADAS commercial position:** Mobileye reported an **$24.5 billion eight-year expected automotive-revenue pipeline** at year-end 2025, up 42% from its prior year-end-2022 update; the company cited program wins in ADAS, expansion within Volkswagen brands, Surround ADAS interest, and growing robotaxi demand. [[3]]
- **Technology scale:** More than **230 million vehicles** had been built with Mobileye EyeQ technology through 2025. [[2]]

**Intel stake/control:** Intel acquired Mobileye in 2017 and, despite Mobileye’s 2022 public listing, remains the controlling shareholder. [[4]] As of December 27, 2025, Intel beneficially owned **50.0 million Class A shares** plus **all 597.8 million Class B shares**, equating to approximately **79.5% of outstanding common stock** and **97.3% of voting power**. [[4]] The disproportionate control reflects Mobileye’s dual-class structure: Class B shares carry **10 votes each**, versus one vote per Class A share. [[4]]

**Bottom line:** Mobileye is separately traded but not independently controlled: Intel retains decisive voting control, while Mobileye’s revenue base is predominantly tied to ADAS and autonomous-driving technology content supplied to automakers. [[1]] [[4]]
